message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**What the 10-K showed (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024):**
- Total net sales: $391.0B, up 2% from $383.3B
- Gross margin: $180.7B (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%)
- Operating income: $123.2B, up from $114.3B
- **Net income: $93.736B** (down from $96.995B) — the decline was driven almost entirely by a one-time, non-cash-like tax charge of $10.2B net related to the European Commission's State Aid Decision, which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7%
- Diluted EPS: $6.08; operating cash flow: $118.3B
- Services revenue grew 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin, offsetting flat iPhone sales and an 8% decline in Greater China
- $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities; $95.0B of stock repurchased in the year

**What I did:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask). The underlying operating business improved — record revenue, expanding gross margin, and operating income up 8% — while the headline net income dip to $93.736B is attributable to the one-time $10.2B State Aid tax charge rather than any deterioration in operations, which I read as a favorable setup. I therefore placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for a total of $9,812 — within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, with a limit price essentially at the market. The order is a buy of a permitted ticker, and no funds were moved out of the account (cash was $50,000 before the trade; the existing 100 MSFT shares were untouched).
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Under $10,000. Total today $9,812 < $20,000. Good.

Summary paragraph.
